note: Reference values for the closed-form power calculations. 'unrounded' is the continuous n the solver returns; 'n' is the integer sample size. Sources are published tables / package documentation that report these figures, or a hand derivation from the cited formula.

solve_n.name: two-sample t, d=0.5
solve_n.source: Cohen (1988) power tables; G*Power 3.1 and R pwr::pwr.t.test report n = 63.77 per group, rounded up to 64

solve_n.name: one-way ANOVA, 3 groups, f=0.25
solve_n.source: pwr::pwr.anova.test(k=3, f=0.25, power=0.8) documents n = 52.40 per group (G*Power total N = 159)

solve_n.name: regression, f2=0.15, 3 predictors
solve_n.source: pwr::pwr.f2.test(u=3, f2=0.15, power=0.8) gives v = 72.71, N = v + u + 1; G*Power reports total N = 77

solve_n.name: two proportions, h=0.3
solve_n.source: pwr::pwr.2p.test(h=0.3, power=0.8) documents n = 174.42 per group

solve_n.name: equivalence (TOST), margin 0.5 sd, true difference 0
solve_n.source: Chow, Shao & Wang: n = 2 (z_0.95 + z_0.9)^2 / 0.5^2 = 68.5 per group; the exact-t TOST figure is slightly larger

solve_effect.name: smallest detectable d at n=50 per group
solve_effect.source: G*Power 3.1 sensitivity analysis, two-sample t, n1 = n2 = 50, power 0.8: d = 0.566

correct.name: Benjamini-Hochberg
correct.source: hand derivation: p*m/rank = 0.02,0.02,0.04,0.04; running minimum from the largest

correct.name: Hochberg
correct.source: hand derivation: sorted p times 4,3,2,1 = 0.02,0.03,0.06,0.04; running minimum from the largest = 0.02,0.03,0.04,0.04

effect_size.name: d to r
effect_size.source: r = d / sqrt(d^2 + 4) for equal groups
